t: Fire programme: retention ₹25 lakh; 1st surplus 20 lines; 2nd surplus 12 lines; facultative obligatory ₹5 crore; balance facultative. On a risk of sum insured ₹16 crore a claim of ₹96 lakh is paid. The 1st surplus treaty's share is
e: 1st surplus = 20 × ₹25 lakh = ₹5 crore = 5/16 of the risk; share = 5/16 × ₹96 lakh = ₹30 lakh (retention 1.5, 2nd surplus 18, F/O 30, facultative 16.5).

t: In the same programme (SI ₹16 crore; retention ₹25 lakh; 1st surplus 20 lines; 2nd surplus 12 lines; F/O ₹5 crore) the facultative reinsurer's share of the ₹96 lakh claim is
e: Automatic capacity = 0.25 + 5 + 3 + 5 = ₹13.25 crore, leaving ₹2.75 crore facultative = 2.75/16 of the risk; 2.75/16 × 96 = ₹16.5 lakh.

t: An insurer retains ₹1 crore and has a 1st surplus of 15 lines. To accept risks of sum insured up to ₹25 crore without facultative support, its 2nd surplus treaty must have at least
e: Retention 1 + 1st surplus 15 = ₹16 crore; the 2nd surplus must absorb ₹9 crore = 9 lines of ₹1 crore each.

t: A risk with original premium ₹1,50,000 is ceded 60% to the surplus treaty, which allows 30% ceding commission. The net premium payable to the surplus reinsurers is
An XL cover of ₹1 crore xs ₹20 lakh is shared by reinsurer A (60%) and reinsurer B (40%). A ground-up loss of ₹1.5 crore occurs. Reinsurer B pays
e: Loss above priority = ₹1.3 crore but the layer limit is ₹1 crore; B pays 40% of ₹1 crore = ₹40 lakh. The cedant bears ₹20 lakh priority plus ₹30 lakh above the layer.

t: A stop loss cover pays 90% of losses in excess of a 75% loss ratio. Premium is ₹120 crore and losses ₹105 crore. The cedant's net loss after recovery is
e: 75% of 120 = ₹90 crore; excess ₹15 crore; recovery 90% = ₹13.5 crore. Cedant's net loss = 105 − 13.5 = ₹91.5 crore.

t: Facilities (PML basis): retention ₹50 lakh; quota share 20% max ₹2 crore; 1st surplus 20 lines max ₹10 crore; 2nd surplus 15 lines max ₹7.5 crore. A risk of SI ₹60 crore is written at 40% PML. The facultative placement is
e: PML amount ₹24 crore: retention 0.5; QS 20% = 4.8 but max 2; 1st surplus 20 × 0.5 = 10; 2nd surplus 15 × 0.5 = 7.5. Total ₹20 crore; facultative ₹4 crore.

t: A policy for annual premium ₹12,000 is issued on 1 January. On 31 March the amounts of earned and unearned premium are respectively
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Written premium ₹12,000 is booked at issue; three of twelve months have expired, so earned premium is ₹3,000 and unearned premium (reserve for unexpired risk) is ₹9,000.

t: Five-year GNPI ₹50 crore; losses to the XL layer ₹2 crore; rate = burning cost × 100/70, minimum 4.5%, maximum 7%; current GNPI ₹14 crore. The XL premium is
e: Burning cost 2/50 = 4%; loaded 4 × 100/70 = 5.714%, within the band. Premium = 5.714% × ₹14 crore = ₹80 lakh.

topic: Excess of loss premium - minimum rate
t: GNPI ₹20 crore; losses to the XL cover ₹30 lakh; rate 100/75 of burning cost, minimum 3%. The XL premium is
e: Burning cost = 30/2000 = 1.5%; loaded = 2%, which is below the 3% minimum. Premium = 3% of ₹20 crore = ₹60 lakh.

t: An XL cover of ₹1.5 crore xs ₹50 lakh has an annual premium of ₹9 lakh and two reinstatements at 100% pro rata to amount. Two losses produce recoveries of ₹1.5 crore and ₹90 lakh. Total reinstatement premium is
e: First loss exhausts the limit: RP = 150/150 × 9 = ₹9 lakh. Second: 90/150 × 9 = ₹5.4 lakh. Total ₹14.4 lakh.

topic: Reinstatement premium - pro rata to time
t: Treaty 1.4.2024 to 31.3.2025; cover ₹50 lakh xs ₹10 lakh; XL premium ₹1,00,000; a loss on 1.7.2024 gives a recovery of ₹25 lakh; one reinstatement at 100% pro rata to amount and time. The reinstatement premium is approximately
On an XL cover the final premium is ₹16 lakh, the reinstatement premium ₹64,000 and the year's recovery ₹14 lakh. A reinsurer with a 5% share ends the year with a
e: 5% share: premium 80,000 + reinstatement 3,200 = ₹83,200 received; loss paid 70,000; net profit ₹13,200.

t: A buffer XL of ₹1 crore xs ₹25 lakh has an aggregate deductible of ₹40 lakh. Ground-up losses: ₹65 lakh, ₹45 lakh and ₹90 lakh. Total recovery is
e: Excess over ₹25 lakh: 40, 20 and 65. The first ₹40 lakh is absorbed by the aggregate deductible; reinsurers pay 20 + 65 = ₹85 lakh.

topic: Catastrophe excess of loss - hours clause
t: A cat XL of ₹2 crore xs ₹50 lakh per loss occurrence has a 72-hours clause for windstorm. A cyclone lasts 100 hours: losses in the first 72 hours ₹1.8 crore and in the remaining 28 hours ₹70 lakh. Recovery is
e: Two occurrences: 180 − 50 = ₹1.3 crore and 70 − 50 = ₹20 lakh; total ₹1.5 crore. The cedant may choose the start of the 72-hour period to maximise recovery.

t: Treaty account (100%): premium ₹4,00,000; commission 40%; taxes ₹8,000; claims paid ₹1,50,000 (including a cash loss of ₹50,000 already remitted by reinsurers); premium reserve retained 40%; previous year's reserve released ₹1,50,000 with interest at 6%; XL premium for common account ₹3,000; common account XL recoveries ₹7,000. The balance due to a reinsurer with a 30% share is
Profit commission is 20% on the three-year average system. Results: year 1 profit ₹10 lakh; year 2 profit ₹4 lakh; year 3 loss ₹20 lakh. Profit commission for year 3 is
o: nil, as the three-year average is a loss of ₹2 lakh
e: Average = (10 + 4 − 20)/3 = −₹2 lakh. No profit commission is payable on a negative average.

t: Retention on a risk is ₹10 lakh and the sum insured is ₹65 lakh. The cession to the surplus treaty amounts to
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Surplus = ₹65 − ₹10 = ₹55 lakh; expressed in lines of ₹10 lakh this is 5.5 lines. Lines need not be whole numbers.

t: A treaty in its first year: premium ₹40 lakh; commission 30%; claims paid ₹6 lakh; outstanding claims ₹4 lakh; management expenses 5%; clean-cut withdrawal at 40% of premium and 90% of outstanding losses. Profit commission at 20% is
e: Outgo = 12 + 6 + 2 + 16 + 3.6 = ₹39.6 lakh against income ₹40 lakh (no portfolio entry in the first year). Profit ₹0.4 lakh × 20% = ₹8,000.

t: Premium ceded ₹2 crore; net profit ₹30 lakh; profit commission 20% on profit up to 10% of premium and 75% on the balance. Total profit commission is
e: 10% of premium = ₹20 lakh → 20% = ₹4 lakh; balance ₹10 lakh → 75% = ₹7.5 lakh; total ₹11.5 lakh.

t: Premiums ceded ₹5,00,000; premium reserve brought forward ₹1,80,000; premium reserve carried forward ₹2,10,000. Earned premium is
The obligatory cession to the Indian reinsurer for 2008-09 was
e: It was 20% up to 2006-07, 15% in 2007-08 and 10% from 2008-09 (continuing in 2011-12), later 5% and now 4%.

t: Under a surplus treaty the limit of the ceding insurer's own liability (its retention) is decided by
e: The cedant fixes its retention schedule; the treaty then provides capacity in lines above that retention.

t: When a loss exceeds both the retention and the limit of an excess of loss treaty, the amount above the limit
o: is paid by the reinsurer in any case
e: The XL reinsurer's liability is capped at the layer limit; any excess falls back on the cedant unless a higher layer has been bought.

t: For outward treaties placed abroad by an Indian insurer, stamp duty under the Indian Stamp Act is payable on
o: no copy, as the document is executed abroad
e: The copy of the outward treaty retained in India must be stamped; inward treaties from foreign cedants must also be stamped in India.

t: About 25% of the world's aviation insurance business is written at
e: Lloyd's of London has historically carried roughly a quarter of world aviation business, with professional reinsurers taking the rest.

t: In the same programme (sum insured ₹24 crore; retention ₹40 lakh; 1st surplus 15 lines; 2nd surplus 10 lines; facultative obligatory ₹8 crore), the amount that has to be placed by facultative reinsurance is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Automatic capacity = ₹0.40 + ₹6 + ₹4 + ₹8 crore = ₹18.4 crore. Balance ₹24 − ₹18.4 = ₹5.6 crore must be reinsured facultatively.

t: Long-tail liability, where claims emerge years after the policy period, is characteristic of
o: products liability, professional indemnity and workmen's compensation
e: Liability classes have long reporting and settlement tails, making IBNR, loss development and index clauses important in their reinsurance.

t: Reinsurance commission is paid by the
e: Ceding commission is allowed by the reinsurer on premium ceded to reimburse the cedant's acquisition costs, taxes and overheads.

t: Which of the following does NOT appear on the income (credit) side of a profit commission statement?
e: Income comprises premiums and the portfolio entries brought forward; management expenses, commission, claims and reserves carried forward are outgo.

t: Which of the following is NOT one of the records maintained for managing an inward reinsurance account?
e: Inward account management relies on accounting flow charts, cash loss and outstanding claims registers and systematic checking of accounts; the cedant's agents are not the reinsurer's concern.

t: Where two reinsurers each take one-half of a ₹10 crore excess over a ₹1 crore retention on a risk, and a loss of ₹5 crore occurs, under 'contributing excess' each reinsurer pays
e: Excess loss = 5 − 1 = ₹4 crore; each contributes in proportion to its participation, i.e. ₹2 crore apiece.

t: A ceding insurer may take credit in its financial statements for unearned premium and unpaid claims on risks reinsured when the reinsurance is placed with
e: Only reinsurance with admitted reinsurers (or non-admitted reinsurance adequately collateralised) qualifies for reserve credit.

t: A plan permitting adjustment of the final reinsurance premium or commission on the basis of actual loss experience, subject to minimum and maximum limits, is
e: Retrospective rating (as in burning cost with min/max, or sliding scale commission) ties the final price to the treaty's own results.

t: A cedant without any automatic treaty for engineering business receives a large erection risk. It must protect itself through
o: facultative reinsurance, since no treaty is at its disposal
e: Facultative reinsurance is the only route where no treaty exists for the class or the risk falls outside treaty scope.

t: Nomination and assignment of a life insurance policy are governed respectively by which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 39 deals with nomination; Section 38 with assignment and transfer.

t: Under proportional facultative reinsurance
o: the reinsurer receives its proportionate share of premium and pays the same share of losses to the cedant
all losses on the risk are transferred to the reinsurer
the reinsurer pays the original insured directly
e: The facultative reinsurer takes a proportion of the risk, premium and losses; it has no contract with, and makes no payment to, the original insured.

t: In reinsurance the word 'treaty' means
o: an agreement between two parties covering a class of business on an obligatory basis
e: A treaty is a general reinsurance agreement, obligatory on both sides, covering all risks of the defined class rather than individual risks.

t: A cedant has both a quota share treaty and an XL cover. The XL wording provides that it protects only the cedant's net retained lines. A loss of ₹2 crore on a risk 50% ceded to the quota share is tested against the XL priority at
e: The net retained lines clause confines the XL to the cedant's net account after other reinsurances, so only ₹1 crore (the retained half) counts towards the priority.

t: After a treaty is in force, the party responsible to the original policyholder for payment of a claim is
e: There is no privity between policyholder and reinsurer; the cedant settles the claim and then recovers from its reinsurers.

t: Reinsurers examine the cedant's outstanding claims at the year end mainly in order to
o: estimate the provisions to be made in their own revenue account
e: Outstanding loss advices at anniversary dates allow the reinsurer to reserve properly and to judge the adequacy of claim reserves.

t: Reinsurers collect and analyse large amounts of data from cedants in order to
o: obtain better terms, balance cessions and strengthen relationships
e: Statistics support renewal negotiations, cash-flow monitoring, portfolio balancing and the follow-up of reserve adequacy.

t: Reinsurers prefer mature financial markets because they
o: offer tax exemption on all premiums
provide good quality customers, easy raising of resources and easy access
e: Mature markets combine quality cedants, capital availability and accessibility; factors like inflation, arbitration and infrastructure also influence entry decisions.

t: A quota share treaty is cancelled on a run-off basis at 31 December. A policy ceded in October suffers a loss the following May. The outgoing reinsurer
o: is not liable, as the treaty has ended
is liable only if the cedant pays a reinstatement premium
remains liable, since on run-off its liability continues until each ceded policy expires
e: Under run-off (natural expiry) cancellation the reinsurer stays on risk for policies ceded before termination until they expire; under clean-cut the liability would have been transferred.

t: IRDAI was constituted under the:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The IRDA Act 1999 established the Authority; it began functioning in April 2000 and is headquartered in Hyderabad.

t: The method of commission under which the agreed percentage is simply applied to premiums ceded, less returns and cancellations, making accounting very easy, is
e: Flat rate commission is fixed irrespective of results and is the simplest to administer; sliding scale and profit commission depend on experience.

t: A ceding insurer withholds a premium reserve of 40% of ceded premium as a deposit. Under normal treaty terms the cedant
o: pays the deposit to the broker
keeps the deposit permanently as a fee
charges the reinsurer interest for holding its money
pays interest on the deposit to the reinsurer and releases it in the following year's account
e: The deposit secures the reinsurer's unearned premium/outstanding loss obligations; the cedant usually pays interest and releases the deposit a year later.

t: Under an XL treaty where the ultimate net loss definition includes loss expenses, legal costs of ₹5 lakh on a claim of ₹60 lakh against a priority of ₹25 lakh are
o: ignored for the purpose of the XL recovery
added to the loss, making the UNL ₹65 lakh and the recovery ₹40 lakh within the limit
e: Where loss expenses form part of UNL, they are added to the indemnity before applying the priority, so the recovery becomes ₹65 − 25 = ₹40 lakh (subject to the limit).

t: A reinsurer receives a cash loss call of ₹2 crore from a cedant on its inward treaty. The purpose of the reinsurer's cash loss register is to
o: record the advance paid so that it is set against the claim when it appears in the periodical account
e: Cash losses are paid in advance of the account; the register ensures the reinsurer credits itself when the claim is later included in the treaty account.

t: A professional reinsurer that has accepted a large inward surplus treaty protects its own retained share through a further reinsurance. This transaction is
e: Retrocession is the reinsurance of reinsurance: the reinsurer (retrocedant) cedes part of its assumed liability to a retrocessionaire.
